name: Timothy Ododo Professional Portfolio & API Service
tagline: Production-ready Go net/http web service and portfolio with zero-dependency architecture
shortDescription: Engineered a high-performance Go web application and REST API adhering to idiomatic standards, sub-millisecond response times, and production deployment on Render.
overview: A robust, lightweight, and clean personal website and API engine designed to demonstrate idiomatic Go engineering principles, structured logging, secure header middlewares, and zero-framework frontend rendering for maximum speed and accessibility.
problem: Many developer portfolios rely on heavy client-side JavaScript frameworks (React/Next.js) resulting in slow initial load times on restricted mobile networks, excessive hydration overhead, and opaque backend mechanics that fail to showcase actual systems programming skill.
solution: Built a clean Go web service using only the Go Standard Library (net/http, html/template, embed, log/slog, encoding/json). All static assets and structured JSON models are compiled and served with sub-5ms latency, complete with secure headers, health monitoring endpoints, and responsive vanilla web views.
keyFeatures: Zero external runtime framework dependencies — 100% Go Standard Library.
Embedded file systems and dynamic template caching with live environment hot-reloads.
Comprehensive /health monitoring endpoint and sanitized JSON contact validation endpoint.
Accessible WCAG 2.2 AA compliant UI with persistent light/dark/system theming.
Fully containerised with multi-stage Docker build producing a sub-20MB production image.
architecture: Layered architecture featuring decoupled handlers, models, and service abstractions. The entry point (cmd/web/main.go) initialises structured slog logging, sets read/write timeouts, attaches HTTP middleware (compression, security headers, rate limiting, request logging), and registers clean REST routes.

stack.Frontend: Semantic HTML5, Modular CSS3, Vanilla ES6+ JavaScript
stack.Infrastructure: Docker (Alpine multi-stage), Render Web Service, GitHub Actions CI

challenges: Handling custom dynamic routes such as /projects/{slug} using Go's standard ServeMux while ensuring strict path validation, proper 404/500 graceful degradation, and cross-platform template resolution across local dev and containerised environments.
solutionApproach: Leveraged Go 1.22 enhanced routing patterns (GET /projects/{slug}) alongside dedicated content service lookup functions that cache JSON data in memory on startup with thread-safe reads.
learnings: Gained deep appreciation for Go's stdlib performance, memory footprint efficiency, and the ergonomics of log/slog for structured observability without third-party loggers.
futureImprovements: Add webhook notifications for contact messages and automated sitemap generation upon content updates.

name: Raspberry Pi Pico Physical Computing Lab
tagline: MicroPython hardware lab & sensor integration curriculum for 200+ students
shortDescription: Designed and deployed embedded hardware demonstrations, sensor drivers, and interactive physical computing exercises for secondary school students at Buildathon Holiday Camp.
overview: Curriculum codebases, hardware diagrams, and interactive MicroPython modules developed for training over 200 secondary school students in embedded electronics and physical computing.
problem: Introducing hardware programming to beginners often hits barriers due to complex C/C++ toolchains, fragile wiring setups, and abstract documentation that discourages young learners.
solution: Developed modular, self-contained MicroPython scripts covering GPIO input/output, PWM LED dimming, ultrasonic distance sensing, and buzzer melodies with clear visual wiring schematics and guided debugging checklists.
keyFeatures: Plug-and-play MicroPython modules with instant visual and auditory feedback.
Clear step-by-step breadboard wiring guides tested for classroom environments.
Defensive coding practices in MicroPython to prevent hardware hangs and short circuits.
Classroom-tested debugging routines enabling students to diagnose their own wiring errors.
architecture: Structured educational scripts with clear separation of hardware initialization (pin mapping), sensor polling loops, and event-driven reactions.

stack.Hardware: Raspberry Pi Pico / Pico H (RP2040 microcontroller)

challenges: Mastering the Pico microcontroller ecosystem, GPIO electrical characteristics, and MicroPython libraries from scratch within 3 days prior to camp deployment, then adapting the content for high schoolers.
solutionApproach: Created an intensive 72-hour prototyping schedule: built test circuits for every lab module, documented common learner failure points, and developed visual analogies for voltage, resistance, and digital vs. analog signals.
learnings: Proved that rapid technical adaptability combined with strong communication skills enables immediate impact in demanding technical education environments.
futureImprovements: Publish open-source interactive web simulators for breadboard circuit planning.

name: SysInspect: Cross-Platform IT Diagnostics CLI
tagline: Automated system triage & network diagnostic tool for IT support technicians
shortDescription: Built a command-line diagnostic utility in Python and Go that automates system hardware audits, network connectivity checks, disk health analysis, and log aggregation.
overview: A fast diagnostic CLI tool created to streamline Tier 1 & 2 IT support triage by executing multi-point health checks across OS processes, memory limits, DNS resolution, and hardware interfaces.
problem: Manual workstation and server troubleshooting requires executing dozens of disparate commands (ping, netstat, df, journalctl, dmesg, ipconfig), consuming valuable support time and leading to inconsistent issue logging.
solution: Created an automated CLI tool that executes concurrent health probes, generates structured Markdown/JSON diagnostic reports, and flags anomalies (packet loss, high disk utilization, failing DNS servers, stale services).
keyFeatures: Concurrent network interface verification and DNS latency benchmarking.
OS kernel log scanner highlighting memory leaks, drive SMART errors, and network disconnects.
One-click diagnostic summary exportable to JSON or terminal-formatted tables.
Cross-platform support for Linux distributions (Debian/Ubuntu/CentOS) and Windows.
architecture: CLI pipeline built with modular diagnostic probes running concurrently via worker goroutines, aggregating metrics into a centralized inspection struct.
challenges: Ensuring deterministic execution across systems without root/administrator privileges while handling platform-specific socket and filesystem disparities.
solutionApproach: Implemented graceful capability fallbacks: probing unprivileged sockets and /proc filesystems when superuser privileges are absent.
learnings: Solidified practical systems administration and network diagnostic workflows learned throughout the Google IT Support Professional certificate.
futureImprovements: Add remote agent telemetry reporting over secure gRPC or HTTPS.

name: SID Event Onboarding & Inquiry Assistant
tagline: High-volume inquiry triage and participant verification engine for Anambra Innovation Week
shortDescription: Created an automated registration validation and attendee inquiry support toolkit helping manage 1,000+ participants during Anambra Innovation Week 2024.
overview: A support operations toolkit built to handle high-traffic participant inquiries, verify registration credentials in real time, and triage support tickets for the Solution Innovation District.
problem: During large government innovation events with thousands of attendees, support teams face inundation from duplicate questions, invalid credential submissions, and slow manual lookup processes.
solution: Developed a lightweight attendee lookup service with automated email confirmation verifiers and categorized FAQ matching powered by AI-assisted classification scripts.
keyFeatures: Sub-second participant verification by ticket ID, email, or phone number.
Automated FAQ routing system reducing repetitive inquiries by over 60%.
Audit logging for credential issuance and check-in status updates.
Responsive mobile-friendly dashboard for onsite event staff volunteers.
architecture: Node.js REST API connected to a normalized relational database with query caching for instant lookups during peak registration surges.

stack.Integration: Event webhook listeners, AI text categoriser

challenges: Managing concurrent read spikes during morning event check-in without degraded database connection pool performance.
solutionApproach: Optimised database indexing on attendee identifier columns and implemented in-memory caching for frequently validated badge codes.
learnings: Understood the critical link between user support empathy, resilient backend architecture, and high-stakes operational execution.
futureImprovements: Incorporate offline QR code cryptographic verification for low-connectivity event halls.

name: Microservices Cloud & CI/CD Deployment Blueprint
tagline: Dockerised multi-service environment with automated GitHub Actions & Azure deployment
shortDescription: Engineered an end-to-end containerized microservices blueprint featuring automated CI/CD pipeline, health checks, reverse proxy routing, and cloud hosting.
overview: A hands-on reference implementation demonstrating modern DevOps workflows: containerizing Go backend APIs, orchestrating with Docker Compose, and deploying through continuous integration.
problem: Transitioning applications from local development machines to scalable cloud instances frequently suffers from 'it works on my machine' configuration drift.
solution: Built automated build pipelines utilizing multi-stage Docker builds, environment secret injection, linting, and zero-downtime deployment triggers.
keyFeatures: Optimised multi-stage Dockerfiles achieving minimal final image sizes.
Automated GitHub Actions workflows with linting, unit testing, and vulnerability scanning.
Nginx reverse proxy configuration with TLS/SSL headers and rate-limiting rules.
Infrastructure setup documentation for Azure App Services and Google Cloud Run.
architecture: Client requests flow through an Nginx reverse proxy gateway to stateless Go container instances with centralized logging and health checks.
challenges: Minimising build artifact sizes and secrets exposure in CI/CD pipeline runs.
solutionApproach: Used Alpine Linux scratch layers for Go binaries and configured secure GitHub repository secret scoping.
learnings: Direct application of principles gained during the 3MTT DevOps cohort and independent cloud engineering projects.
futureImprovements: Add Terraform infrastructure-as-code manifests for automated cloud resource provisioning.

name: PromptCraft: AI-Assisted Code Refactoring & Doc Engine
tagline: Developer utility for automated documentation generation & code explanation
shortDescription: Built a developer tool that ingests code files, parses AST tokens, and generates structured explanations, docstrings, and test cases using AI models.
overview: A developer productivity utility that leverages LLMs responsibly to accelerate code comprehension, documentation generation, and unit test scaffolding.
problem: Writing comprehensive documentation and boilerplate test suites for legacy codebases is time-consuming and often neglected in fast-moving developer workflows.
solution: Created an intelligent CLI and API pipeline that analyzes code functions, generates docstrings following language conventions, and suggests edge-case unit tests.
keyFeatures: Context-aware prompt orchestration with strict temperature and token controls.
Multi-language support for Go, Python, JavaScript, and PHP.
Generates idiomatic unit test templates matching project structure.
Privacy-first design ensuring local file sanitization before prompt dispatch.
architecture: Pipeline parser extracts function signatures and doc comments, formats structured prompts to LLM endpoints, and writes validated responses back to source files.
challenges: Preventing hallucinated function signatures and ensuring generated tests strictly match actual function contracts.
solutionApproach: Injected language AST schemas into system prompts and ran syntax validation linters on model outputs before presenting to developers.
learnings: Mastered techniques for AI-native development: treating AI as an intelligent assistant while maintaining strict human-in-the-loop verification.
futureImprovements: Develop a lightweight VS Code extension wrapper.
